newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania postpones land restitution bill.
newsitem.headline: Romania postpones land restitution bill.

text.p: Romania's parliament on Tuesday postponed approval of a law to ease the return of land seized from pre-war owners during 50 years of communist rule, a key element of the government's market reforms.

The ruling centrist coalition called off the vote in the upper house, the Senate, after too few of its members turned up to ensure passage. The law, already passed by the lower house, will be examined again when parliament reconvenes in September.

The bill amends a land law from 1991, two years after the collapse of communism, with the coalition's main partner, the National Peasant Party, increasing to 50 hectares (125 acres), the maximum entitlement subject to restitution.
The present law only allows the return of a maximum 10 hectares (25 acres).
The government has pledged a series of reforms to eliminate chaos in post-communist agriculture, allowing in particular larger land holdings to improve efficiency.
The issue sparked a row last month between the Peasant Party and its junior coalition partner, the Democratic Party, which initially opposed increasing the amount of land to be returned.
The leftist opposition, thrown out of office in last November's general election, opposes the new law on grounds that it would restore big land-owning interests.
Ex-president Ion Iliescu, defeated last year by reformist Emil Constantinescu, made restitution a key issue of his campaign, saying the centrists wanted to restore Romania's pre-war "land barons".
